title: Consumer Data Right: open banking
summary: The four major banks had to share consumer-authorised data on cards and deposit accounts from 1 July 2020 and on mortgages from 1 November 2020; other banks followed from 1 July 2021.

instruments.title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Consumer Data Right) Act 2019
instruments.provisions: Competition and Consumer Act 2010 Part IVD

instruments.title: Competition and Consumer (Consumer Data Right) Rules 2020

commenced.what: Major banks: phase 1 products (cards, deposit and transaction accounts)

direction_rationale: Portable account data lower search and switching costs, so customers can compare offers and move to challengers.
comparison: Major versus non-major banks during the year between their start dates

verified.notes: Dates from the CDR phasing table (January 2021).

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 18 October 2026 (legislation gap scan, docs/legislation_gap_scan.md) from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use. 'alicia dates' reports 'differs': the Rules' own commencement is not dated in the as-made text; data-sharing obligations for the major banks began on 1 July 2020 under the Rules' phasing schedule, which is the effective date used.

assessment.summary: Banks must share customers' data, with consent, with accredited providers. Portable data should make it easier to compare and switch, and lets new services be built; take-up has been slow and compliance costs high.

marks.reason: Portable account data lower search and switching costs.
Data access lets new firms build comparison and other services.
Banks bear substantial build and compliance costs for the data-sharing system.

responsible.note: Administers the Competition and Consumer Act 2010 (except Parts given to other Ministers).

history.what: Consumer data sharing extended to the energy sector, starting with the largest retailers.
